issues.display_title: Issue #1402: Different Duration of Binary Pano Level Source on CLI and Build App
issues.main_description_html:
Description

There is a difference in processing duration of the Pano Level source binary when it is executed directly via the CLI versus when it runs through the built Photo Studio app. This task is to document and verify the root cause of that difference.

Developer Result Video

(Detect Pitch Roll)

(Generate Auto Level)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2104abb4-02d8-4ab8-afaf-b4649dbb967c

The video shows that Photo Studio duration is slightly longer, with a 1-second difference. After the generation process, the metadata is copied from the source to the generated file to preserve the original metadata.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-requisites

  • A 360° equirectangular source image with known, non-empty metadata (GPS lat/long, camera make/model, and pano/projection XMP tags).
  • The standalone Pano Level binary available for CLI execution.
  • The built Photo Studio app installed.

Steps

  1. Inspect and record the source image metadata (GPS, camera, pano tags) using ExifTool.
  2. Run the Pano Level binary directly via CLI on the source image. Record the processing duration. Inspect the output metadata.
  3. Open the same source image in Photo Studio and run the AutoLevel / leveling operation. Record the processing duration. Inspect the output metadata.
  4. Compare the two durations.
  5. Compare the metadata of both outputs against the source.
  6. Compare the visual leveling result (horizon correction) of both outputs.

Expected Results

  • Photo Studio duration is ~1 second longer than the CLI duration.
  • The extra time corresponds to the post-generation metadata copy step.
  • Photo Studio output preserves the original source metadata (GPS, camera, pano/XMP tags).
  • Raw CLI output may be missing some of the original metadata (since it skips the copy step).
  • The leveling (horizon correction) result is visually identical between CLI and app outputs.

Notes for Tester

  • Confirm the difference is consistent across multiple source files (small and large resolution) and not growing disproportionately with file size.
  • Flag if the in-app duration is significantly more than ~1 second longer, as that would indicate a separate performance issue rather than the metadata copy overhead.
